Sections.Name: Access and Online Registration
Sections.Introduction: The access screens introduce the shared sign-in page and the applicant registration workflow. Registration information is submitted for review; a captured form or button does not establish that a membership has already been approved.

Sections.Name: Administrator Interface
Sections.Introduction: The administrator figures show operational summaries, membership records, request review, attendance and camera setup, inventory, transaction monitoring, reports, staff access, and audit review. These screens support administrator responsibilities without granting personal-profile editing rights over existing members.

Sections.Name: Authorized Staff Workspace
Sections.Introduction: The staff figures show the separate workspace for attendance, product sales, counter membership services, and online request review. Its limited member lookup and request summaries support the authorized transaction without providing a general member-profile viewer or inventory-maintenance interface.

Sections.Name: Member Portal
Sections.Introduction: The member figures show personal membership information, renewal requests, attendance, product browsing, and the profile menu. The member remains limited to their own records. Product browsing describes in-store availability rather than an online checkout service.

Sections.Name: Session Confirmation
Sections.Introduction: The final interface figure shows the confirmation used before ending an account session. It is an interaction control rather than an additional main functional requirement.

Figures.Title: Shared Sign-in Interface
Figures.Caption: Figure 6. Shared Sign-in Interface
Figures.Description: The sign-in screen provides the account identifier and password inputs, password visibility control, sign-in action, password-recovery link, and entry point for new-member registration. Members use their email address; assigned staff and administrator identifiers are handled by the supported authentication workflow. The Remember my login option retains the login identifier rather than filling or storing a plaintext password. After successful authentication, the role and account state determine the permitted interface. The screenshot shows the access form and does not demonstrate a completed login or an authorized session.

Figures.Title: Online Membership Registration Form
Figures.Caption: Figure 7. Online Membership Registration Form
Figures.Description: The complete online registration form shows personal and emergency-contact information, membership-plan choices and dates, health declarations, optional fitness goals, agreements, a liability waiver, digital-signature capture, and portal email and password fields. The applicant supplies the required information and submits a pending application for authorized staff or administrator review. Selecting a plan or submitting the form does not activate the membership. The whole screenshot preserves the order and overall length of the form; the selected enlarged views that follow make its small fields and submission controls easier to inspect.

Figures.Label: 7a
Figures.Title: Online Membership Registration Form
Figures.Caption: Figure 7a. Online Membership Registration Form - Enlarged detail: Personal, emergency-contact, and membership information
Figures.Description: This enlarged view highlights the personal, emergency-contact, and membership areas of the complete registration form in Figure 7. Separate name inputs identify the applicant, while birth, contact, height, and weight fields record the submitted personal details. The emergency-contact area identifies another person and their relationship to the applicant. The plan and date controls describe the requested membership. These entries remain application information until the authorized review workflow records its decision.

Figures.Label: 7b
Figures.Title: Online Membership Registration Form
Figures.Caption: Figure 7b. Online Membership Registration Form - Enlarged detail: Health declaration, fitness goals, and agreements
Figures.Description: This detail enlarges the registration form's health declarations, optional fitness goals, agreements, and liability waiver. The selections and acknowledgments document information supplied by the applicant for membership review; they are not a diagnosis or a promise of a particular fitness result. Health-related records remain subject to the implemented authorization rules. The complete form remains visible in Figure 7, while this supplementary view helps readers inspect the smaller declaration and acknowledgment controls.

Figures.Label: 7c
Figures.Title: Online Membership Registration Form
Figures.Caption: Figure 7c. Online Membership Registration Form - Enlarged detail: Signature, portal credentials, and submission
Figures.Description: This enlarged detail shows the signature area, portal email, password, confirmation, and application-submission controls. A member account uses email rather than a separately collected username. The applicant completes the required information and acknowledgments before submitting the pending request. Authorized staff or an administrator then reviews the application and confirms the applicable in-person payment before approval. The image illustrates the controls within the complete form in Figure 7; it does not show an approval outcome.

Figures.Title: Administrator Dashboard
Figures.Caption: Figure 8. Administrator Dashboard
Figures.Description: The administrator dashboard provides a quick view of registration requests, current members, the selected day's check-ins and sales, and low-stock items. A request-review shortcut directs the administrator to the appropriate pending requests, while the sidebar opens the operational modules. The lower attendance area summarizes the available visits for the displayed day. These cards help identify work that needs attention before opening a detailed module. The amounts, counts, dates, and records visible in this screenshot are captured interface values and should not be interpreted as evaluated performance results or permanent system totals.

Figures.Title: Active Membership Records
Figures.Caption: Figure 9. Active Membership Records
Figures.Description: The active-membership view lists member records and provides search and plan filters. Each row exposes supported actions such as renewal, active-plan change, and viewing details, while the page also provides the add-member entry point and navigation to expired records and approvals. The administrator can use the limited operational controls to perform a membership transaction or inspect the permitted information. Viewing a member's personal details remains read-only. An association with User Management therefore does not mean that the administrator can directly edit an existing member's personal-profile fields.

Figures.Title: Expired Membership View
Figures.Caption: Figure 10. Expired Membership View
Figures.Description: The Expired tab separates expired membership records from the active list. Search and plan filters help the administrator locate the relevant record before taking a supported membership action. The captured view contains an empty-state message because no recently expired member matches the displayed filters. This state should not be interpreted as a missing module or evidence that the database contains no expired records under every possible query. A renewal is handled through the authorized membership workflow rather than by manually changing the status displayed in this list.

Figures.Title: Online Registration Review
Figures.Caption: Figure 11. Online Registration Review
Figures.Description: The approvals view separates new-registration requests from renewal requests and presents the information available for reviewing a selected application. The captured registration card includes the requested plan, applicable dates, contact and declaration details, signature, request status, and approval or rejection controls. The administrator confirms the applicable payment received at the gym before approving the request. The authorized review operation validates the pending state and records the decision and related membership transaction. Existing applicant authentication and subsequent membership activation are distinct stages; the visible approval button label does not redefine that account sequence.

Figures.Title: Administrator Walk-in Registration
Figures.Caption: Figure 12. Administrator Walk-in Registration
Figures.Description: The administrator's complete Add New Member dialog supports a walk-in registration using personal and emergency-contact details, a membership plan and dates, declarations, signature, and new-member portal credentials. This captured administrator dialog has a full-name input, while the staff add-member screen uses separate name fields. Submission creates the applicable records through the authorized service and records the in-person transaction. It does not provide general editing access to an existing member's profile. The complete dialog is shown first; the following enlarged details support reading its fields without replacing that overview.

Figures.Label: 12a
Figures.Title: Administrator Walk-in Registration
Figures.Caption: Figure 12a. Administrator Walk-in Registration - Enlarged detail: Personal and emergency-contact information
Figures.Description: This detail enlarges the personal and emergency-contact inputs of the administrator's complete walk-in dialog in Figure 12. The captured dialog uses a full-name field, birth and contact information, height and weight, and emergency-contact details. These inputs support creating a new member record through the authorized counter workflow. They are not a general interface for viewing or editing an existing member's personal profile. The staff form's separate-name arrangement is illustrated independently in Figure 26.

Figures.Label: 12b
Figures.Title: Administrator Walk-in Registration
Figures.Caption: Figure 12b. Administrator Walk-in Registration - Enlarged detail: Plan, dates, declarations, and signature
Figures.Description: The enlarged middle area of the administrator's walk-in dialog presents the membership plan, dates, health declarations, fitness goals, and signature capture. The operator records the information supplied for the in-person membership transaction and asks the applicant to provide the required signature. Clear resets that capture when it must be entered again. These controls support the new record and applicable transaction; they do not grant medical-assessment or unrestricted personal-profile editing privileges.

Figures.Label: 12c
Figures.Title: Administrator Walk-in Registration
Figures.Caption: Figure 12c. Administrator Walk-in Registration - Enlarged detail: Portal credentials and record creation
Figures.Description: This detail shows the new member's portal email, password, matching confirmation, and the dialog's final actions. The operator submits the completed walk-in registration through the authorized service, which creates the applicable account, profile, member, and transaction records. The member QR becomes available through the supported workflow. The complete dialog remains the main figure in Figure 12. This enlarged view documents the input and submission controls rather than proving that a particular registration succeeded.

Figures.Title: Administrator Attendance and QR Workspace
Figures.Caption: Figure 13. Administrator Attendance and QR Workspace
Figures.Description: The Attendance & QR workspace provides the scanner entry point, phone-camera pairing information, date selection, and attendance log. An authorized operator scans a member QR to record the applicable check-in or check-out after the service checks the member and visit state. The displayed log is filtered by the selected date; an empty log means no entries are shown for that state. Camera selection and phone-pairing controls are illustrated in the following figures. The screenshot does not show an active camera feed and is not evidence of a completed physical scan.

Figures.Title: Attendance Camera Selection
Figures.Caption: Figure 14. Attendance Camera Selection
Figures.Description: The camera-selection dialog distinguishes a camera connected to the current device from a paired phone camera. Choosing This device starts the local camera workflow, while Phone camera opens the supported pairing workflow. The dialog also communicates the setup-QR expiry and the remembered-pairing period. These are different lifetimes: the setup code is temporary, whereas a completed pairing can remain valid for the configured period unless ended earlier. A paired phone still requires the appropriate operator authentication; pairing alone does not grant attendance-recording or administrator privileges.

Figures.Title: Phone-Camera Setup and Pending Pairing
Figures.Caption: Figure 15. Phone-Camera Setup and Pending Pairing
Figures.Description: The complete phone-pairing dialog brings the setup QR, visibility control, slot counts, phone-limit control, paired-phone list, and pending-QR list into one view. A pending setup QR reserves capacity alongside completed pairings. End pairing removes the selected connection; End QR cancels an unused reservation. Closing the dialog is different from ending a pairing. The setup code links the intended phone and is distinct from a member attendance QR. Pairing does not replace the required operator authentication, and the captured code is not presented as a reusable credential for a later session.

Figures.Title: Pairing Capacity Reached
Figures.Caption: Figure 16. Pairing Capacity Reached
Figures.Description: This pairing-dialog state shows that the configured phone limit has been reached and no free slot is available. The list identifies the paired devices and provides the supported removal controls. The administrator may end an unused pairing or change the permitted phone limit through the authorized settings workflow. The presence of a limit message is an expected capacity-control state, not by itself a camera malfunction. Counts in this capture describe that particular pairing state; they do not establish a tested maximum number of simultaneous system users or verified multi-phone performance.

Figures.Title: Inventory Access Gate
Figures.Caption: Figure 17. Inventory Access Gate
Figures.Description: The Store & Inventory screen is shown before the administrator has opened the protected inventory area. The access gate requests the supported store password and provides the Open Store action. This additional interface state is separate from the account login and does not grant inventory rights to staff or members. The server's role and authorization checks remain necessary even when the interface displays an unlock control. The supplied screenshot illustrates the locked state; the following inventory figure shows the product-management view after the applicable access requirements have been met.

Figures.Title: Administrator Product and Inventory Catalog
Figures.Caption: Figure 18. Administrator Product and Inventory Catalog
Figures.Description: The administrator's complete inventory catalog displays supplement and merchandise cards together with product images, names or variants, configured prices and sale units, stock information, and maintenance controls. Add Product and the supported edit, restock, and archive actions belong to the administrator workflow. The complete capture shows how these controls relate to the full product list. Products can use different units according to their configuration, so the visible unit must be read from the relevant record. Member and staff catalog access does not grant these inventory-maintenance permissions.

Figures.Title: Membership Sales Monitoring
Figures.Caption: Figure 19. Membership Sales Monitoring
Figures.Description: The Membership tab in Sales summarizes recorded membership income and transaction counts. Period and day filters determine which records appear, while the plan-category cards provide a breakdown of the selected results. The captured screen shows an empty transaction result for its filter state even though a broader overall-income card remains visible. These values have different filter contexts and should not be treated as directly interchangeable totals. The page monitors saved membership payments; it does not process an online payment or establish that a customer receipt was issued.

Figures.Title: Product Sales Monitoring
Figures.Caption: Figure 20. Product Sales Monitoring
Figures.Description: The Products tab presents product-income information, including the supplement and merchandise breakdowns for the selected period or day. The New Sale control opens the supported product-sale workflow. Completed sales are recorded with their itemized details and the applicable stock deduction after validation. An empty transaction area indicates that no records match the current filter, rather than proving that no product sales exist. Administrator transaction monitoring is broader than the staff operator's own-sales review, and members do not receive a product-checkout function through this page.

Figures.Title: Administrator Report Selection
Figures.Caption: Figure 21. Administrator Report Selection
Figures.Description: The Reports page organizes report choices into membership, daily operations, and payment-and-sales areas. The visible cards include membership, member status, renewal, archive, attendance, inventory, payment, and sales reports, with filters for the requested scope and period. Selecting a supported report initiates its preview or export workflow. The supplied image shows report selection rather than an opened report preview or final print layout. Report figures must therefore be interpreted as interface navigation, not as evidence of a measured operational improvement or of a particular completed export.

Figures.Title: Staff Account Creation and Directory
Figures.Caption: Figure 22. Staff Account Creation and Directory
Figures.Description: The administrator's Staff Accounts page combines the creation form and staff directory. The form separates first name, optional middle initial, and last name and collects the assigned username, Gmail address, contact and demographic information, password, and confirmation. The directory exposes supported account-details and activation controls. These administrator actions govern staff-account access; they are distinct from a member updating their own personal profile. Although the captured subtitle uses narrower attendance-only wording, the documented staff role also includes the authorized counter, product-sale, and request-review operations illustrated in the staff figures.

Figures.Title: Administrator Activity Logs
Figures.Caption: Figure 23. Administrator Activity Logs
Figures.Description: The complete Activity Logs screen shows the actor, system-area and date filters, Apply and Clear controls, recorded-event rows, refresh action, and pagination. Entries identify the event time, actor, action, affected area or record, and available field-change details. This is an administrator review function. Reading a log entry does not execute the recorded operation, and staff and members do not receive this interface. The whole capture preserves the relationship between the filters, result table, and paging controls; its sample records are not a formal security or performance evaluation.

Figures.Title: Staff Attendance Workspace
Figures.Caption: Figure 24. Staff Attendance Workspace
Figures.Description: The staff attendance workspace shows the scanning entry point and manual QR input beside the permitted visit-history list. The authorized scan operation validates the member and visit state before recording a check-in or check-out. The table displays recorded visit information, including Incomplete status for a previous-day visit without a recorded exit. This attendance access is distinct from viewing or editing a member's personal profile. The complete screenshot preserves the full workspace and visible history. Existing table entries do not independently prove that a new physical camera scan succeeded during documentation preparation.

Figures.Title: Staff Product-Sale Workspace
Figures.Caption: Figure 25. Staff Product-Sale Workspace
Figures.Description: The complete staff Product sales page combines the sale-entry form, the operator's own recent product sales, and the selection catalog. Customer, product, quantity, and unit inputs determine the transaction being submitted. The service validates the selected item and available stock before saving a completed sale and applying the corresponding deduction. Product cards show the permitted prices, units, variants, stock, and availability; unavailable items cannot be selected for a completed sale. The staff role can record sales and review its own product-sale records without receiving product-edit, restock, archive, or unrestricted sales-review permissions.

Figures.Title: Staff Counter Membership Services
Figures.Caption: Figure 26. Staff Counter Membership Services
Figures.Description: The complete staff Membership page places Add Member, Renewal, and Change Plan within the supported counter-service workflow. The displayed add-member form collects separate first name, optional middle initial, and last name, portal credentials, contact and emergency-contact details, a standard membership plan, and the applicant's signature. Create member & record payment submits the authorized walk-in transaction for payment received at the gym. The other actions use their own limited member lookup rather than unrestricted profile access. The whole screen establishes the layout; selected enlarged details follow for its personal-information and submission controls.

Figures.Label: 26a
Figures.Title: Staff Counter Membership Services
Figures.Caption: Figure 26a. Staff Counter Membership Services - Enlarged detail: Walk-in member and portal details
Figures.Description: This enlarged view of Figure 26 makes the staff add-member inputs easier to read. First name, optional middle initial, and last name are collected separately, followed by the new member's portal credentials and contact, birth, and emergency-contact information. The surrounding tabs separate walk-in registration from direct renewal and active-plan change. These authorized counter tasks use the applicable creation or limited-lookup workflow; they do not provide a general personal-profile viewer or editing function for existing members.

Figures.Label: 26b
Figures.Title: Staff Counter Membership Services
Figures.Caption: Figure 26b. Staff Counter Membership Services - Enlarged detail: Standard plan, signature, and transaction submission
Figures.Description: The enlarged lower form shows the standard membership-plan selection, signature area, Clear signature control, and Create member & record payment action. Staff are limited to the plans and prices available to their role. The completed form is submitted for the supported in-person transaction; it does not process an online payment. This detail supplements the complete workspace in Figure 26 and remains distinct from approving a previously submitted online registration or renewal request.

Figures.Title: Staff Online Request Approval
Figures.Caption: Figure 27. Staff Online Request Approval
Figures.Description: The Requests approval tab lists pending online registration and renewal summaries with only the information needed for the staff review decision. The operator confirms the applicable payment received at the gym and approves or rejects the selected request. The authorized review function rechecks the active role and pending state and prevents competing decisions from processing the same request twice. This limited request card is not a member-profile viewer. Its presence confirms that request review is a staff function within the documented scope, while administrator-only inventory, reporting, pairing, and staff-account controls remain outside this workspace.

Figures.Title: Staff Account Menu
Figures.Caption: Figure 28. Staff Account Menu
Figures.Description: The staff account menu identifies the signed-in operator and provides the available light or dark appearance selection and logout action. Theme selection changes the presentation of the workspace, not the account's role or permitted operations. The captured staff menu does not expose the member Update Profile action or administrator management modules. The label and controls therefore support account awareness and session navigation while the application's authorization rules continue to restrict operational access. The logout action is illustrated separately by the final confirmation dialog.

Figures.Title: Member Membership Progress and Renewal
Figures.Caption: Figure 29. Member Membership Progress and Renewal
Figures.Description: The member view presents the current plan, membership expiry, remaining days, and elapsed-membership indicators. This progress describes the passage of the membership period rather than workout performance, weight change, or a clinical fitness measure. The renewal area allows the member to choose a supported plan and submit an online renewal request for review. Submission does not immediately change the membership dates or approve the payment. An authorized staff member or administrator reviews the request, and an approved active renewal preserves the applicable unused membership time under the documented renewal rule.

Figures.Title: Member Dashboard, Attendance, and In-store Catalog
Figures.Caption: Figure 30. Member Dashboard, Attendance, and In-store Catalog
Figures.Description: The complete member dashboard combines the member's own membership progress, renewal controls, attendance, Show QR Code entry point, and in-store product catalog. Progress concerns elapsed membership time rather than exercise performance or physical change. Attendance is limited to the member's own visits. The QR button opens the personal code for use by an authorized attendance operator; the capture shows that button rather than the opened code. Catalog cards support product browsing at the gym and do not provide online checkout or inventory maintenance. The whole screenshot preserves the full page and its naturally empty areas.

Figures.Title: Member Profile and Appearance Menu
Figures.Caption: Figure 31. Member Profile and Appearance Menu
Figures.Description: The member menu provides Update Profile, appearance selection, and logout. Update Profile leads to the permitted personal self-service workflow for the signed-in member, not a staff or administrator account-management interface. The menu screenshot shows the entry point rather than the opened edit form, so it should not be captioned as a complete profile-editing screen. The member may update only their own permitted details under the implemented validation and authorization rules. Theme selection affects appearance, while logout ends the account session through the supported confirmation flow.

Figures.Title: Logout Confirmation Dialog
Figures.Caption: Figure 32. Logout Confirmation Dialog
Figures.Description: The logout dialog asks the account holder to confirm whether to end the current session. Cancel returns to the current interface, while Log out proceeds with the supported sign-out workflow. This confirmation reduces accidental navigation away from an active workspace but does not substitute for authentication or authorization. The picture is a captured interaction state, not an additional main function beyond the nine functional requirements. Remembering a login identifier is separate from retaining an authenticated session; confirming logout does not reveal a stored password or sign an account back in automatically.
